The assembler was loading trays onto the overhead rack at the sub assembly station. The task was routine scheduled work. Stage of the task: in process - normal running work. Method in effect: SW-402 Sub Assembly Tray Handling. The task was being performed as written. Equipment involved: Overhead tray rack at sub assembly station 2. Equipment state at the time: at rest or stopped. Equipment condition: modified from original. Detail: The rack was raised by about 4 inches during a layout change two months ago. The object handled weighed 10 to 25 lb. Handling difficulty: medium - needs two hands. It was held both hands and by handles or hand holds. PPE in use: safety glasses and general purpose gloves. This matched the PPE specified for the task. The event was not witnessed and was self reported later. The task is performed over a hundred times per shift. The assembler has performed this task for six months to two years. One cycle consists of the following: lift a tray from the cart at waist height, raise it with both arms extended to the rack at shoulder height, push it forward about 18 inches onto the rails, then lower the arms and turn back to the cart. Posture held during the task: reaching overhead. The task requires moderate force. Symptom onset: Aching across the front of the right shoulder first noticed about six weeks ago, at first only towards the end of a shift. Since then the symptoms are worse and now present outside work. Recent change in the work: The rack was raised by about 4 inches during a layout change roughly two months ago, and the tray count per shift went from 140 to 180 at the same time. The condition arose from repetitive motion or sustained posture. Motion involved: Repeated overhead reach with the right arm raised above shoulder height and the elbow extended through the push onto the rails. It is repeated over a hundred times per shift. Each repetition takes moderate force. Difference from a normal run of this task: The rack height and the tray count both changed about two months ago and the station has not been reassessed since. Conditions at the point of injury: nothing notable. The event occurred in the second half of the shift. No overtime was being worked. It happened within several hours in. The assembler had performed this task before. No known hazard, prior near miss, open action or risk assessment covers this task. No guard, interlock, barrier or control was bypassed, missing, defeated or ineffective. Stop-work opportunity: The symptoms could have been reported when first noticed six weeks ago, but they were mild and were expected to settle. At the scene, no first aid was given at the scene. No first aid was given at the scene. Notified: the team lead and EHS. This happened at the end of the shift. Reason for the delay in reporting: the aching was mild at first and was expected to settle with rest over the weekend. Afterwards, nothing was secured. Work at the location continued in a modified way. The assembler was sent to an offsite occupational clinic for evaluation.
